## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`status()` cuts the revision to 7 characters, but its own docstring says it uses the same identifier as `history()`, which shows 12. Fix this before merge, because the running status line won't match the history and completion lines for the same deployment.

## Changes
The PR adds `status(revision, attempt)` and `attempt_label(attempt)` to `app/display.py`, which build a "Running: <revision> (attempt N)" line. It also adds two tests in `tests/test_display.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/display.py:14 — correctness — Use `revision[:12]` in status to match history — For the test's `REVISION`, `status()` prints `Running: 0123456` while `history()` and `completed()` print `0123456789ab`. `short_revision = revision[:7]` contradicts the docstring at line 13, "using the same identifier as history." — Users and operators who match a running deployment against its history or completion line by revision see two different short identifiers. — Fix: Change the slice to `revision[:12]` and make `test_running_status_contains_attempt` assert the full expected string; its current `startswith`/`endswith` checks never look at the revision.
